## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.

The changing distance between the satellites is used to infer shifts in mass. Those inferred shifts help scientists investigate changes in water stored as groundwater, in lakes and rivers, in soil moisture, and in glaciers and ice sheets. They can also reveal sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
